title: Hosted SSE reconnect policy and partial-chunk reconciliation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Multiple customers reported truncated or duplicated SSE streaming responses after intermittent TCP disconnects. Symptoms differ across clients: some observe steady partial-chunk duplication, others see missing tails of responses and then a sudden short backfill. This ticket centralizes the investigation and implements a server-side reconnect and chunk-reconciliation policy for hosted API streams so customer apps observe fewer partial outputs and are able to recover without manual retry hacks.
reproduction_steps: 1) Use hosted API streaming endpoint with message-level sequence IDs enabled in header
2) Send a long streaming generation (>= 1024 tokens) with continuous SSE output
3) Inject a TCP disconnect at random token boundary (simulate flaky network)
4) Reconnect client immediately and resume stream using existing client resume token
5) Observe either duplicated chunks, truncated final tokens, or out-of-order chunks depending on timing and client backoff behavior
root_cause_summary: Race between server token emission and connection teardown + weak resume handshake semantics. Server sometimes assigns sequence numbers before KV cache commit and, on quick reconnects, will replay in-flight chunks or drop final partial buffer. Client resume token lacks definitive last-ack offset, so reconciliation relies on best-effort matching which fails in edge timings.
proposed_fixes: Add server-side durable stream-offset ack: persist last-committed token offset before emitting 'event: data' boundary
Introduce explicit resume-handshake: client includes last-seen-offset and server returns canonical next-offset; if mismatch, server emits backfill of missing tokens instead of blind replay
Change SSE buffering to flush safe-chunk boundaries only (avoid splitting multibyte tokens across events)
Add lightweight idempotency markers on each chunk (stream-uuid + sequence) to dedupe out-of-order replays
Compatibility mode: opt-in header for Dedicated/Private that keeps old behavior for on-prem customers during rollout
rollout_plan: 1) Implement durable offset ack and handshake in staging behind feature flag
2) Run regression tests and chaos network test suite (10k short disconnects simulated)
3) Canary deploy to 5% of hosted traffic with header opt-in for affected customers
4) Monitor dedupe rate, backfill frequency, and customer error reports for 72 hours
5) Gradual ramp to 100% with kill-switch and incremental metrics gating
rollback_plan: Disable feature-flag and revert runtime routing to previous emitter. If partial rollbacks required, toggle canary masks per-region until effect is mitigated. Emergency revert PR ready: runtime/revert/ENG-24876. Notify affected customers when rollback occurs.
qa_checks: Integration test: simulated reconnect with randomized offsets validates backfill/seq correctness
E2E with official JS and Python SDKs ensuring resume-handshake flows pass
Load test to validate no increase in median latency (<= +10ms target)
telemetry_queries: customer_errors_query: logs("sse:protocol-mismatch OR sse:unexpected-truncation") | group_by(customer_id) | top(50)
notes: 2026-03-06: Early analysis shows two failure modes: replay duplication and final-chunk drop.
Trade-off: persisting offset before emit adds a small latency increase; we scoped to <= 10ms median to limit customer impact.
PM preference: prefer server-side fix over client SDK changes to reduce customer coordination.
SRE input: require extra retention of stream-events for 48h for postmortem debugging
